#### Overview

* Alex (founder, Acme) spoke with Darius, a staff claims adjuster on small business liability, about where evidence and tooling fall short on a claim and what a new product could supply

* Slip and fall is the largest injury bucket on his small business desk, and the first **three days** carry the file: recorded statements, an investigator for footage, sweep logs, the lease and the policy

* His day-one asks: a state and county deadline lookup, prewritten statement questions by loss type, and an investigation checklist that builds itself

* Footage is the strongest evidence he gets but is absent or useless on most small business files, roughly **seven in ten**; big chains do better at about half to two thirds

* Carriers buy fewer platform modules for commercial lines than for personal lines, so commercial adjusters lean on wikis, binders and web searches

* Acme has no product yet and is still exploring lending, fintech and insurance

#### First days of a slip and fall

* Darius calls everyone who was present within **three days** and records each statement, then sends a contracted investigator for footage before the DVR loops

* He asks for cleaning logs, recent contractor work and the lease, and reads the coverage early

* On a severe injury he flags the account underwriter and asks for prior loss runs

#### Represented vs. unrepresented claimants

* Unrepresented claims close in about **four months**; once a lawyer is retained, **18 months to 3 years**

* Lawyers keep prior injury history closed until a suit forces discovery, and representation raises the cost of the claim on its own

#### Gaps on day one

* State and county rules on acknowledgment and coverage letters decide bad faith exposure later, and missed deadlines surface years on in depositions

* The internal wiki, binders and shared drive disagree, so he often learns deadlines from plaintiff firm websites

* Outside AI tools are barred by compliance; the carrier is piloting its own tool

* A note-taking agent for **45-minute** lawyer negotiations would save about **20 minutes** of write-up each time

#### Video evidence

* Clean video settles negligence; recordings are often grainy and overwritten before late reports arrive

* Repeat claimants know the camera gaps and fall inside them

* Stores send whole afternoons of footage; he wants a tool that marks the exact minute of the fall

#### Claims platforms and AI

* Guidewire is the long-standing claims platform; many "in house" systems are reskinned Guidewire

* Duck Creek came up as a platform Darius knows by name only

* From freelance work with Benchline, he sees agents handle single tasks but fail on long chains of steps

* He expects AI to take busywork off adjusters rather than replace them
